summary: Reddit, X and Bluesky were unreachable today, so this is a smaller report built only from Hacker News threads I could read in full. The strongest themes are developers losing paid AI quota to failed requests and silent model quality drift, plus fatigue from supervising many parallel coding agents and teams quietly dropping code review.

ideas.title: AI Quota Loss Ledger
ideas.oneLiner: A local tracker that shows how much of your Claude or other AI plan limit was burned by failed, retried or runaway requests.
ideas.problem: Paid AI plans meter usage in 5-hour and weekly pools. Users report that failed requests still consume the limit, that retry restarts the task and spends more, and that the usage bars they relied on sometimes disappear. They cannot tell where the quota went.
ideas.targetUsers: Heavy Claude Code / Claude web users on Pro and Max plans, and developers who use several AI coding tools.
ideas.monetization: Free CLI plus a one-time or small monthly Pro tier (about $3-5/month) for history, alerts and multi-provider support.
mvp: Read local Claude Code session logs and compute tokens per session and per day
Flag sessions that ended in errors or retries and total the wasted tokens
Show a live weekly-pool burn-down with a projected run-out time
Desktop or menu-bar alert at 50/80/95% of the weekly pool
Export a CSV for an evidence-backed support ticket

competitors.name: LimitPilot — Claude Usage Tracker
competitors.gap: Browser gauge for session and weekly limits; it shows the number but not which requests wasted quota (per its store listing; I did not test it).

competitors.name: Claude Usage Meter
competitors.gap: Strip above the composer showing session, weekly and Fable usage; I could not verify that it attributes loss to failed requests.

sources.quote: the bar showing the usage for the 5h-Limit in the settings/usage modal AND the listing of "5h Limit usage" in Claude Code (/usage) is also vanished.

ideas.title: Model Drift Canary
ideas.oneLiner: Run your own fixed prompts against your AI coding model every day and get an alert when quality or token appetite shifts.
ideas.problem: Every few weeks developers feel their model got worse (more forgetful, more verbose, ignoring corrections), but nobody can prove it. Public benchmarks don't match their own prompts and they cannot tell a real change from an A/B test or a bad day.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers and small teams who rely on Claude, GPT or similar models for daily coding work and pay per seat or per token.
ideas.monetization: Free for 3 canary prompts; $9/month for unlimited prompts, multiple models and Slack/email alerts.
mvp: Define 5-20 canary prompts with expected checks (tests pass, JSON schema, exact-match)
Scheduled daily runs against chosen models through the user's own API key
Track pass rate, response length and token usage over time on one chart
Alert when a metric moves beyond a rolling baseline
Shareable report page to attach to a vendor support ticket

competitors.name: BridgeBench nerf-bench
competitors.gap: Publishes daily public benchmark results for a model, but not your own prompts, so it cannot confirm a regression in your workflow (surfaced in the HN thread; I did not test it).

ideas.title: Parallel Agent Cockpit
ideas.oneLiner: One calm dashboard that shows what each running coding agent is doing, what needs your decision, and what changed in shared memory.
ideas.problem: Developers now supervise several agents at once. They report decision fatigue, context switching and a flood of generated text to review, and multiple agents overwrite a shared memory file with no trace of who changed what.
ideas.targetUsers: Developers running two or more AI coding agents in parallel, especially solo founders and small teams.
ideas.monetization: Free for 2 concurrent agents; $12/month Pro for unlimited agents, notifications and history.
mvp: Detect running agent sessions (terminal/tmux/log files) and list state: working, waiting for input, errored, done
Single queue of pending approvals with the relevant diff or command inline
Versioned shared-notes file with per-agent attribution and one-click revert
Desktop and phone notification only when an agent needs a decision
Daily summary of what each agent finished

competitors.name: herdr
competitors.gap: A terminal multiplexer for agents that an HN commenter said they use a lot; I did not evaluate it and cannot say what gap remains beyond what commenters describe.

sources.title: Ask HN: Are you tired too in this AI era?

sources.title: Ask HN: Are you tired too in this AI era? (comment by fabioborellini)

sources.title: Ask HN: What is your best hack to keep your agent's context in sync?
sources.quote: One of the problems I face is multiple agents writing to a common memory which can lead to unwanted memory overwrites without any trace.

ideas.title: No-Review Merge Safety Net
ideas.oneLiner: A GitHub app that records which merges skipped human review, risk-scores them, and produces the audit trail compliance asks for.
ideas.problem: Teams are quietly dropping code review because AI speeds up writing code, while security people report AI-built apps full of holes. Leaders still worry about SOC 2 evidence. Nothing tracks the gap between 'we agreed to merge without review' and what actually shipped.
ideas.targetUsers: Small engineering teams (5-50 devs) that use AI heavily and need SOC 2 or customer security questionnaires.
ideas.monetization: $29/month per org for up to 10 repos; $99/month for audit exports and Slack digests.
mvp: GitHub App that lists merged PRs with no approving review
Risk score per PR (touches auth, secrets, dependencies, infra, size)
Weekly digest of unreviewed high-risk merges to a Slack channel
Policy file: which paths always require review
Exportable audit CSV for compliance evidence

competitors.name: CodeRabbit
competitors.gap: Does AI review itself; it doesn't track or report the merges where humans skipped review (from general knowledge; not verified today).

competitors.name: Vanta
competitors.gap: Compliance automation that can check review rules but is heavyweight and expensive for small teams (from general knowledge; not verified today).
